pages.transcription:
Hotel Wyndham
Newyork, June 2nd, 41

Dear Hanna
I return the enclosed forms signed and quite
agree with you that you should be able to take any necessary
steps or precautions. Your last letter (from May 21st) proves that our
thoughts still conform. As soon as we had mailed you the power of
attorney we regretted that we had omitted to specify it also for
safes, and on the other hand we wrote you just yesterday that
Stefan is not quite happy with Eisen's effusive and evasive
letter and that it seems to us that he puts Stefan's interest
behind that of newly acquired friends and clients, in an
understandable and yet disappointing instinct of self-interest.
I am very glad that you too are now convinced that Eva is in
satisfactory surroundings and somehow I am absolutely certain
that all along you would have acted in the same way about
her as we did. You, too, would have made the arrangement
with Salmon's last year under the special circumstances and
the personal and general uncertainty then prevailing, and you,
too, would have transferred her to Amity Hall on our return.
And you, too, would still now be uncertain whether the Public
or the Private School has greater educational advantages. Miss
Baker promised to let me know when she comes to Newyork and
I hope to discuss this question with her, as well as with
several others. As the Private School will not reopen before the
end of September there is plenty of time also for you to write
me suggestions and your opinion, although in the end I am afraid
you must still leave the decision to us. I can understand how you
miss Eva - I judge it from the fact how much I miss you -
but somehow for this very reason I enjoy so much having
Eva here and looking after her as well as I can. In a way it
is a compensation and gives me the feeling that our old life
has not been completely disrupted but continues, for the time
being, over here. (Stefan will criticize these last remarks as being
imprecise, but after all I am no writer and I hope that even
you will understand what I try to say and not speak again of
"burdening us with Eva's care". - I am terribly sorry that this
torture at the dentist is still dragging on. Both you and Manfred
will have earned a long rest in Bath, and I hope you get it soon.
please turn over
love and kisses Lotte.
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf Hotelpapier. Am linken Rand vertikal geschrieben: 'Stefan has written to the Bank Manager, thanking him for all the help he has given you. We heard that Bohem[?] was again with you, either in Bath or in London. Manfred must soon become an expert in X-Ray science.' Am rechten Rand vertikal geschrieben: 'Trlor[?] Father, Herr Hofman and other people we really like. And among them Hanne Kohl, Balbui[?] Raes, Poto Roda, we will give tomorrow a cocktail for all the refugees-friends, there will be, I am afraid, a whole crowd'.

pages.transcription:
I had to-day a reply from Washington that they do not more cable enquiries
to their embassy in London, but that they have written them and asked to
send me a report about the status of your brother's affidavit - in clear
language that probably means that I shall never hear from them.
For why should the London consulate take the trouble to write me a
letter when they refuse to give an answer to the people themselves?
Probably too many people have tried to find out how things stand
via cables from Washington and they therefore stopped this practise.
